scope: Corollary 3.2 (Solenoidal rapid forcing on the torus) of the manuscript “Computation under Rapidly Vanishing Navier–Stokes Forcing” (preprints/Computation-under-Rapidly-Vanishing-Navier-Stokes-Forcing-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 931c07840228968b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a positive computable viscosity. From any deterministic Turing machine M and finite input w, one can effectively construct on the unit flat torus T3 a smooth, solenoidal, spatially mean-zero force satisfying all the bounds (5) with T3 in place of R3, with zero initial velocity, such that the unique smooth solution satisfies M halts on w ⇐⇒ 1 4 < X1(t, a∗) < 3 8 for some t ≥ 0, a∗ = (1/2, 1/4, 1/2). Here the inequality denotes the indicated open coordinate slab of the torus. Pressure is normalized to mean zero, and uniqueness holds in the classical periodic class of Section 2. The velocity and all its mixed derivatives also decrease faster than every inverse power of time.
